title: Exposing C++ to Blueprints 🔗
description: Make variables and functions editable and callable from Blueprint graphs.

slides.title: Blueprint-C++ Synergy 🤝
slides.content:
# Two Languages, One Game

The true power of Unreal comes from mixing C++ and Blueprints. You write base classes in C++ and extend them in Blueprints. Designers can tweak values without touching code.

We'll make a C++ class that is fully configurable in the editor and callable from Blueprint graphs.

slides.title: Expose a Variable 📊
slides.content:
## Health Example

In header:
```cpp
UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadWrite, Category = "Combat")
float MaxHealth = 100.0f;

UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly)
float CurrentHealth;
```
* `EditAnywhere` → appears in Details panel (defaults and instances).
* `BlueprintReadWrite` → get/set nodes in Blueprints.
* `Category` → groups under "Combat" header.
* `BlueprintReadOnly` → only get node, no set (for internal tracking).

Now in any Blueprint child of this class, you can read/write MaxHealth, but only read CurrentHealth.

quizData.question: Which specifier makes a variable appear in the Details panel and editable?
quizData.explanation: EditAnywhere enables editing in the property editor. VisibleAnywhere only shows, not editable.

slides.title: BlueprintCallable Functions 📞
slides.content:
## Public API

```cpp
UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Combat")
void Heal(float HealAmount);
```
In .cpp:
```cpp
void AMyActor::Heal(float HealAmount)
{
    CurrentHealth = FMath::Min(CurrentHealth + HealAmount, MaxHealth);
}
```
Now in any Blueprint, you can drag from an execution line and search "Heal". It appears as a node!

For functions that just return data without side effects, add `BlueprintPure` to avoid execution pins.

quizData.question: A BlueprintPure function appears with an execution pin and a return value pin.
quizData.explanation: BlueprintPure functions have only data pins; they are evaluated on demand, like a math expression.

slides.title: BlueprintImplementableEvent vs BlueprintNativeEvent 🎭
slides.content:
## Let Blueprints Override

* **BlueprintImplementableEvent** – no C++ body; the function is **implemented entirely in Blueprints**. It's like a placeholder that Blueprint must fill.
  ```cpp
  UFUNCTION(BlueprintImplementableEvent)
  void OnDeath();
  ```
* **BlueprintNativeEvent** – you provide a default C++ implementation (`_Implementation` suffix), but Blueprints can override it.
  ```cpp
  UFUNCTION(BlueprintNativeEvent)
  void OnDamaged(float Damage);
  // In .cpp:
  void AMyActor::OnDamaged_Implementation(float Damage) { ... }
  ```
These are perfect for events that gameplay code triggers, allowing designers to add visual feedback in Blueprints.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use BlueprintNativeEvent for Extensibility

Expose key events (e.g., OnActivated) as BlueprintNativeEvent. C++ handles logic, but Blueprint can add sound effects or particles.
